## Item 1 — Delete account: Play Console Data Safety web setup

- **Status:** PLANNED — booked 2026-07-18. **Non-code** — Alvin executes with Claude's guidance when he's ready. **No grilling needed** — this is compliance paperwork (a static page + a Play Console form field), not a design decision; every design call for account deletion itself was already made in [ADR-0045](../adr/0045-delete-account-hard-delete-rpc.md).
- **Request:** the in-app deletion RPC + client teardown shipped in [v1.6.5.md Item 6](v1.6.5.md#item-6--delete-account-play-policy-requirement-) (`9e0614e`+`22d7cc1`, on-device verified), but Google Play's Data Safety policy also requires two things that live outside the app: (1) a publicly reachable "Delete my account" web page, and (2) the Play Console → App content → Data safety form's account-deletion URL pointing at it. Both still pending, flagged as "Alvin, manual" in the v1.6.5/v1.6.6 write-ups.
- **Guide (when we sit down to do it):** draft a static `delete-account.html` on the existing `alvinleyble.github.io/ipon-love-legal` GitHub Pages site (sibling to `privacy-policy.html`), describing the in-app self-service path (Settings → Profile → Delete account) and what gets removed (per ADR-0045 — full cascade, no retained data, immediate). Push it to the `ipon-love-legal` repo, then fill in the Play Console Data Safety form's deletion-URL field. No app code changes.
- **Verify:** page loads publicly at the URL; Play Console form saves without validation errors.

## Item 5 — Archived-category confirm-on-archive warning (related to deferred Item 23)

- **Status:** PLANNED — booked 2026-07-18, **needs a grill before build.** **Model (once grilled): TBD** — likely Sonnet, low–medium effort (a confirmation dialog + an existing-transactions check, following the Item 16/26 dialog precedent).
- **Related, not a duplicate:** [deferred.md Item 23](deferred.md#item-23--archived-entity-label-fallback-in-records--budgets-️-deferred--needs-tester-feedback) **stays deferred as-is** — it's about *display-time* behavior for a category that's already archived (does its old Records/Budgets rows keep the real name, or read "Uncategorized"?), and Alvin still wants tester feedback on that before deciding. This item takes a different angle at the same root problem: instead of waiting to see how the degraded label reads after the fact, **warn the user at archive time** if the category has existing transactions — Alvin's proposed copy: *"This category has existing transactions and will become Uncategorized when archived."*
- **Why both:** resolving this one doesn't retire Item 23 — a category archived *before* this ships (or if the user proceeds past the warning) still needs Item 23's display-time decision. They're complementary: this is the upfront-informed-consent leg, Item 23 is the after-the-fact-display leg.
- **Open design questions for the grill:** exact copy (Alvin's draft above, or shorter); does the same warning fire for archiving an **account** (Item 23 covers both account and category labels); does it also warn about a **budget** referencing the category (Item 23 covers Budgets too); is this a blocking confirm (must acknowledge) or a dismissable snackbar; and — worth surfacing explicitly at grill time — telling the user upfront "it becomes Uncategorized" implicitly leans Item 23 toward keeping the Uncategorized-fallback behavior (vs. Analysis-style label preservation), so this grill may end up resolving Item 23's open question too.
- **Not yet designed** — do not build until grilled.

## Item 8 — "Playful Pop" visual identity redesign (multi-slice arc)

- **⚠️ HARD RULE (Alvin, 2026-07-20):** this is a **pure reskin — change the look only, NEVER remove anything.** Every existing figure, control, caption, row, and behavior must survive; only styling changes. If the 1e mockup omits an element the current screen has (e.g. the net-assets header figure), **recreate it in the new style, don't drop it.** This overrides "go accurately with the design" whenever the two conflict on an element's *presence* (not its appearance). See memory `feedback-playful-pop-pure-reskin-no-removal`.
- **Status:** IN PROGRESS — booked 2026-07-20, **GRILLED 2026-07-20** (design resolved, see "Grilled design" below). **Model: Opus, high effort** — genuinely novel + cross-cutting: a new global shape/style axis the color-only theme system can't express today, spanning ~20 screens and interacting with the theme system (ADR-0014), the S9 palette-gating, and the navbar (ADR-0017/0026). No schema/Room change (pure UI/theme — stays **v26**; the icon-library migration keeps DB icon keys stable → no data migration). **Multi-slice arc — sub-slices logged under "Slice plan" below.**
- **Request (Alvin, 2026-07-20, via the `.design_handoff_1e_playful_pop/` bundle — `README.md` + `1e Playful Pop.html`, 4 hi-fi screens):** implement the "1e Playful Pop" direction — an expressive evolution of the current M3 look: **asymmetric "leaf" squircle corners, subtle rotations on hero elements, heart-tipped progress bars, hearts as accent glyphs** (legend bullets, date-header bullets, progress tips, Shared badges, split-bar knot), a restyled donut (57% hole, ~1.8° gaps), and a restyled bottom nav (pink-pill active slot, −4° rotated FAB). High-fidelity — colors, type sizes, radii, spacing are final in the HTML (exact inline values at a 360dp reference frame).
- **Resolved scope (Alvin, via `/book` clarifying questions 2026-07-20):**
  - **Integration = "Replace app identity."** The Playful Pop **shape language becomes the app's new default identity, applied globally** — *not* a selectable palette/style toggle. Replaces the global `IponShapes` M3 look.
  - **The 6 color palettes are RETAINED and the design ADAPTS to them.** The HTML's hardcoded blush `#FBE5EE` / deep-plum `#8B2A57` / pink-accent `#F48FB1` tokens must map onto **semantic `ColorScheme` roles** so that picking Rose / Mauve / Lavender / Peach / Sage / Mocha re-tints the entire Playful Pop look. **Nothing color-specific may be hardcoded** to the sample's blush-on-plum.
  - **Light mode required.** The sample is dark-only; every token needs a light-mode counterpart driven by the existing `isDark` flag. Both light + dark must ship.
  - Corollary: the shape/style language itself is **not** premium-gated (it's the default identity, free for everyone); only the existing color palettes keep their S9 gating (Rose/Peach free, rest premium) — unchanged.
- **NOT an IA change (confirmed):** the design's "Analysis · Records · ⊕ · Manage · More" nav already matches our existing model (reorderable pins + fixed center ⊕ Add + More, ADR-0017/0026) — it's one pin config illustrated, not a restructure. The handoff README's "nav structure unchanged" holds. Tab/screen content is unchanged throughout — reskin + layout refinement only. No new state (README §State Management): same data sources, percent chips derive from existing aggregates.
- **Grilled design (2026-07-20 — all forks resolved):**
  1. **Color sourcing = a derived `PlayfulColors` layer, NOT new raw palette tokens.** A `PlayfulColors` object exposed via `LocalPlayfulColors`, computed inside `IponTheme` from the *active* `ColorScheme` + `isDark`. One formula adapts all 6 palettes × light/dark; palettes stay the single source of truth; ADR-0014's live-preview/Apply flow is untouched (it already swaps the `ColorScheme`, the derived layer just recomputes). Rejected the ~24 hand-tuned per-palette raw constants (maintenance tax, easy to drift).
  2. **Mode-aware surface mapping** (the crux — `blush` is always the *lighter/softer* accent card, `deepPlum` always the *stronger/darker* one; the relationship holds in both modes):

     | Playful surface | Light source | Dark source |
     |---|---|---|
     | `accent`/`onAccent` | `primary`/`onPrimary` | `primary`/`onPrimary` |
     | `blush` (bright card) | `primaryContainer` | `lerp(primaryContainer, white, .85)` |
     | `onBlush` | `onPrimaryContainer` | `onPrimary` (dark ink ≈ `#4A1229`) |
     | `deepPlum` (strong card) | `primary` | `primaryContainer` |
     | `onDeepPlum` | `onPrimary` | `onPrimaryContainer` |
     | `glass` (rows) | `primary` @ .06–.08 | `primary` @ .06–.08 |
     | `background` gradient | subtle: `lerp(bg, primaryContainer, .10)` → `bg` | plum: `lerp(bg, primary, .12)` → `bg` |
  3. **Shapes = bespoke leaf-squircle helpers, global `IponShapes` stays conservative.** New `LeafShapes` in `core/ui/theme/` — `leafShape(big, small)` → `RoundedCornerShape(topStart=big, topEnd=small, bottomEnd=big, bottomStart=small)`, a `mirrored` variant, and an `index % 2` selector for alternating rows. Applied only to cards/rows/chips/badges/nav/FAB. Global `MaterialTheme.shapes` left sane so dialogs/sheets/text-fields don't get warped corners (keeps the incremental rollout safe — un-migrated screens keep working).
  4. **Rotations kept; only animations gated on reduced-motion.** Static tilts always on (identity; ≤1° on text-bearing cards, larger angles only on non-text decorative elements: FAB −4°, icon squircles ±4°, title heart −8°, nav-pill −4°). A `LocalReducedMotion` boolean (from `Settings.Global.ANIMATOR_DURATION_SCALE == 0`), baked in from Slice 1, makes the *animations* (chip radius/color morph ~200ms, progress-heart spring, FAB press scale/rotate) **snap** when reduced.
  5. **Semantic money colors = fixed, mode-aware `SemanticColors`** (negative/positive/income), the same across all 6 palettes (green = income regardless of theme), each with a light + dark value: negative dark `#FF97A8` / light `~#C62828`; positive & income dark use light greens (`#8FD8A8`) / light use `#2E7D4F`. Replaces today's scattered hardcoded `IncomeColor = #2E7D32` + `colorScheme.error` usages — migrated per-screen (un-migrated screens keep current colors until their slice). Negatives keep the app's existing `-₱x,xxx.xx` formatting.
  6. **Icons = actual Material Symbols Rounded (FILL 1) vector drawables** (not the webfont, not the older `Icons.Filled.*` drawing) for design accuracy — Alvin: "even the assets." The **entire category/account icon library migrates at once** ([IconRegistry.kt](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/core/ui/icons/IconRegistry.kt), ~50 glyphs): swap the `ImageVector` *values* to Symbols vector drawables while keeping the string keys stable (`"food"`, `"rent"`…) → **no DB/schema change**. Any single glyph that can't be reproduced faithfully gets flagged, not silently substituted.
  7. **Partner colors** (Wifey `#F06292` / Hubby `#5B8DEF`) stay the existing `accent_color` attribution (ADR-0014) — unchanged.
  8. **Shared components (infra slice):** `LeafShapes` helpers, `PlayfulCard` (blush/plum/glass variants w/ tilt), `HeartTippedProgress` (clamped heart tip), heart-accent glyph, the leaf-pill chip (shared Analysis/Manage/Couple), the restyled bottom nav (pink-pill active slot + −4° FAB, **visuals only** — no nav-restore/deep-link/pin logic touched in `IponApp.kt`), and the gradient backdrop.
- **Slice plan (arc — logged here as each lands):**
  1. **Infra + global frame + Analysis·Donut** — **✅ DONE `f570463`** (2026-07-20, Opus, on-device verified: Rose light + Rose dark + Sage dark, adaptivity proven — the whole look re-tints per palette with zero hardcoded blush-on-plum). `PlayfulColors`/`LocalPlayfulColors` derived layer + `SemanticColors`, `LeafShapes`, `LocalReducedMotion` wired into `IponTheme` (global M3 shapes kept conservative); shared components `PlayfulCard`/`HeartTippedProgress`(+`HeartProgressMath`)/`PlayfulChip`/`playfulBackground()`/`PlayfulScreenTitle`+`HeartBullet`; custom pink-pill bottom bar + rotated squircle FAB in [IponApp.kt](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/navigation/IponApp.kt) (visuals only — all switchTab/ADD/More handlers + coach targets preserved) + gradient backdrop; full Analysis·Donut screen (tilted title, leaf-pill period/view chips, blush hero, donut at 57% hole with heart center, 2×2 glass category grid w/ heart bullets, "All N categories" expand pill). **Net-assets header figure retained** (recreated in the Playful title's actions slot) per the pure-reskin hard rule after it was first dropped. +`LeafShapesTest` +`HeartProgressMathTest`. No schema/Room change (v26). Note: Analysis·Donut uses heart bullets, **not** category glyphs, so it did not depend on Slice 2.
  2. **IconRegistry → Material Symbols Rounded** — **✅ DONE `5f4028a`** (2026-07-20, Sonnet, medium effort, on-device verified). No schema/Room change (icon keys are DB-stored strings and stayed byte-identical → no data migration; stays **v26**).
     - **Change:** migrated all 43 glyph *values* in [IconRegistry.kt](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/core/ui/icons/IconRegistry.kt) (`CATEGORY_ICONS` 36, `ACCOUNT_ICONS` 15, overlapping — both `Map<String, ImageVector>`) from `Icons.Filled.*` (the older Material Icons drawing) to **Material Symbols Rounded, FILL 1**. Map type and every string key kept identical, so every consumer (`EntityPickerOption`, `IconPicker`, `ACCOUNT_ICONS[key]`, `goalIcon()`/`GOAL_ICONS`) is untouched. **Approach:** new `core/ui/icons/MaterialSymbols.kt` — `msRounded(name, pathData): ImageVector` builds an `ImageVector` via `androidx.compose.ui.graphics.vector.PathParser` (needed an explicit `group` import — the DSL's `group`/`path` are extension functions, not builder members) inside a `group(translationY = 960f)` to remap the MS `0 -960 960 960` viewBox into Compose's top-left-origin `0..960` viewport; `fill = SolidColor(Color.Black)` set explicitly (`Icon()` tints via `ColorFilter` regardless, but a null fill paints nothing). Path strings pulled programmatically (not hand-transcribed) from the `@material-symbols/svg-400` npm package's `rounded/<name>-fill.svg` files, extracted via a small Python script — sourced verbatim from `google/material-design-icons`, one `-fill1` SVG per glyph. **Two glyphs were renamed upstream, same visual match, not a substitution:** `CardGiftcard` → `redeem` (gift box + ribbon), `PhoneAndroid` → `mobile` (phone silhouette); `Business` (the old M2 building glyph, not the briefcase) was resolved to MS `domain` (a semantic pick, since MS has no direct `business` icon and `business_center` is a briefcase — would've collided visually with the already-separate `work` key). No glyph needed the drawable-import fallback or a "can't reproduce faithfully" flag. Removed all `Icons.Filled.*` imports.

Swap those two **color values** to `SemanticColors` (`semantic.income` / `semantic.negative`) — a pure value substitution, not geometry — which also fixes dark-mode legibility (the hardcoded green is a dark green; the semantic dark-mode green is light). Only Canvas **geometry/paths** stay out of scope. `ExpenseFlowChart` needs no semantic swap (its line is `primary`, no income/expense split).
